#### 1. palmoplantar keratoderma-deafness syndrome  —  Tier 1 — Definitive / Highly Plausible  (fitness 0.793)
**Link type:** shared pathway (Reactome:R-HSA-190704, Reactome:R-HSA-190827, Reactome:R-HSA-190861, Reactome:R-HSA-190872)

**Proposed mechanism:** Pathogenic GJB2 variant —DISRUPTS→ GJB2 (HGNC:4284); GJB2 (HGNC:4284) —DISRUPTS→ Gap junction communication (GO:0005845); Gap junction communication (GO:0005845) —LEADS_TO→ Keratosis of palms and soles (HP:0000970); Gap junction communication (GO:0005845) —LEADS_TO→ Sensorineural hearing impairment (HP:0000405); Gap junction communication (GO:0005845) —LEADS_TO→ Leukonychia (HP:0011235). Pathogenic variants in GJB2 disrupt the formation and function of gap junctions, impairing intercellular communication. This disruption leads to the characteristic phenotypes of Bart-Pumphrey syndrome (keratosis of palms and soles, sensorineural hearing impairment, leukonychia) and palmoplantar keratoderma-deafness syndrome (keratosis of palms and soles, sensorineural hearing impairment).

**How to falsify it:** If pathogenic variants in GJB2 are found to be exclusively loss-of-function in one syndrome and exclusively gain-of-function in the other, or if the two syndromes are consistently associated with mutations in entirely different genes with no shared downstream effects, this hypothesis would be falsified.

**Why it matters:** Understanding the shared genetic basis in GJB2 provides a unified target for therapeutic strategies aimed at improving keratinocyte function and hearing in patients with either Bart-Pumphrey syndrome or palmoplantar keratoderma-deafness syndrome. This could involve gene therapy or small molecule approaches to restore connexin-26 function.
